title: Power Apps: modern, refreshed look reaches the mail app on the semi-annual channel
summary: The rollout facts and automatic enablement match Microsoft's roadmap. Hold the briefing because its release-channel guidance confuses feature activation with build delivery, the environment API example is incomplete, and Microsoft does document general automation for the app setting reported as having none.

claims.claim: This Power Apps change extends the Fluent-based modern, refreshed look for model-driven apps to the mail app.
claims.quote: Extends the Fluent-based modern, refreshed look for model-driven apps to the mail app

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Semi-annual releases roll out gradually across region groups on successive weekends, rather than one date for everyone.
claims.quote: Like the monthly channel, each semi-annual release follows the gradual weekly rollout across the same region groups, starting with the first release region and reaching each subsequent region group on the following weekend.

claims.quote: For users in your organization where more training and extensive testing are needed before rollout out of new end user impacting features.

claims.claim: No spend control applies.

claims.claim: The environment channel is under Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Behavior.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Manage. ... select Environments. ... select an environment. ... select Settings. Expand Product, and then select Behavior.

claims.claim: PATCH /organizations(<organizationid>) with the ReleaseChannel column set to the channel value is a runnable channel-setting call.
claims.quote: Update operations use the HTTP PATCH verb. Pass a JSON object containing the properties you want to update to the URI that represents the record.
claims.fix: The pre-check's missing-endpoint lead is a formatting false positive: the Organization reference documents PATCH /organizations(organizationid), logical name releasechannel and value 3 for Semi-annual. Nevertheless replace the prose pseudo-call with 'PATCH [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations(<organizationid>)' and JSON body '{"releasechannel":3}', labelled as the Semi-annual example, with Content-Type: application/json and If-Match: *. Cite the Organization reference and https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/update-delete-entities-using-web-api for the request format.

claims.claim: Updating environment behaviour settings requires the System Administrator security role or equivalent permissions.
claims.quote: Make sure you have the System Administrator security role or equivalent permissions to update the settings.

claims.claim: Per-app channel settings take precedence over the environment channel without qualification.
claims.quote:
3. App release channel value other than Auto (for example, Monthly, Semi-annual).
4. Environment release channel value other than Auto (for example, Monthly, Semi-annual).
claims.fix: Replace the precedence statement in the note, rendered table and prose with 'A configured user channel override takes precedence over app and environment channels. An explicit app release channel other than Auto takes precedence over the environment channel.'

claims.claim: A user channel override takes precedence over app and environment channels.
claims.quote: User channel override takes precedence over the environment channel and app channel.

claims.claim: The effective model-driven app channel depends on environment, app and user configuration.
claims.quote: Release channel can be configured on the environment, app, or user level. The release channel is primarily managed on the environment or app. The user level is an override

claims.claim: When app and environment channels are both Auto, Power Apps and Dynamics 365 environments use Monthly.
claims.quote: App release channel and environment release channel are both Auto. In this case, Power Apps and Dynamics 365 environments use the monthly channel.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The release channel controls when a build arrives.
claims.quote: The release channel controls feature availability. It doesn't change the environment's database version or the platform and application versions deployed to the environment.
claims.fix: Replace 'The release channel controls when a build arrives, not whether the look is applied once it does' with 'The release channel controls feature availability, not the database, platform or application versions deployed to the environment.' Preserve the separate, supported statement that builds roll out to region groups on successive weekends.

claims.claim: An app-specific release channel can be configured in the app designer.
claims.quote: A maker can use the app designer to explicitly set the release channel for an app, which overrides the environment channel.

claims.claim: A user-specific channel override is available in the Power Platform admin center under the environment's Users.
claims.quote: Select Users > See all. ... Under the Model apps channel field, select Change channel. ... Select a channel from User channel override dropdown menu.

claims.claim: A user must refresh the browser tab twice after an environment channel change.
claims.quote: When you change the release channel at the environment level, a user must refresh the browser tab twice to update the release channel information.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with 'Learn's changing-channels page says to refresh the browser tab twice after an environment channel change; its behaviour settings page says users switch after one to two refreshes.' Both pages are already cited.

claims.where: Governance controls: paragraph beginning The environment setting
claims.claim: The behaviour settings page itself documents the per-user channel override under Users.
claims.quote: Select Users > See all. ... Under the Model apps channel field, select Change channel.
claims.fix: Replace 'The same page documents the per-user override under Users in the environment' with 'Learn's User channel override page documents the per-user override under Users in the environment', linking to https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/user-channel-override. The behaviour page documents the environment setting, not a Users path.

claims.claim: Learn documents changing a user's channel through the ReleaseChannel column on UserSettings.
claims.quote: Developers can change the user release channel by updating the ReleaseChannel column value for the row in the UserSettings table.

claims.claim: The cited modern-look article locates New look for model driven apps through Solutions > solution > Add Existing > More > Setting.
claims.quote: Under Solutions, open an existing solution with one or more model-driven apps. ... Select Add Existing > More > Setting. ... Select New look for model driven apps.

claims.claim: The modern-look article describes the New look for model driven apps setting as an admin mechanism for turning off the New Look.
claims.quote: Admins can turn off the New Look for all users by updating the New look for model driven apps app setting.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn's app settings page says the New Look setting is hidden and ignored from 2026 Wave 1, conflicting with the rollback instructions.
claims.quote: This setting is hidden and ignored with the 2026 Wave 1 release when the new look becomes mandatory.

claims.claim: Learn's important changes page says the admin settings related to the classic look will be removed.
claims.quote: The admin settings related to this feature will be removed.

claims.claim: The cited Learn pages do not specifically confirm that the New Look setting controls the mail app.
claims.quote: Searched: mail app modern New look release channel setting; New look for model driven apps API setting SaveSettingValue. Opened modern-fluent-design and app-properties; the mail paragraph states rollout, not applicability of the New Look switch.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table and closing paragraph
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API for the New Look app setting.
claims.quote: Adds or updates the setting app value for the current app or the setting environment value for the current environment. ... You can also use the following Web APIs to get or update a setting value ... SaveSettingValue action
claims.fix: Replace the null side with kind 'other', call 'Xrm.Utility.getGlobalContext().saveSettingValue("<setting-unique-name>", false, {overrideScope: 2}).then(successCallback, errorCallback)' and docs https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/clientapi/get-update-setting-value-using-code. Retain the qualification that this is general app-setting automation, not confirmation of a working mail-app rollback. Replace the no-API prose with 'Learn documents generic app-setting automation; its effect on the mail app is not confirmed.'

claims.claim: The New Look setting does not control release timing.
claims.quote: Searched: New look for model driven apps release timing; mail app modern New look release channel setting. Opened modern-fluent-design, app-properties and channel-overview; none explicitly states this negative claim about the setting.
claims.fix: Remove 'It does not control release timing' from the control note and rendered table. The separate, verified description of release channels already explains feature availability.

claims.quote:
